Commentary.Commentary: New Zealand have now got a good lead and they would now look to put in a better show with the bat. Sri Lanka on the other hand, need to take wickets and that too quickly if they are to get back in the game. Will we see the host continue their domination or will the visitors fight back.

Not a lot you can write about the Lankan batting. They could not cope against the swing and have been bowled out very cheaply in their first innings. Only three batsmen managed to score in double digits but none could make it big. Angelo Mathews fought hard but ran out of partners in the end.

An excellent bowling performance from the Kiwi pacers here! They did not post a big first innings score but their bowlers have led right from the front. It was Southee at the start who ran through the top order. De Grandhomme dismissed the hero of the last game and Boult this morning took the remaining 6 in the 5 overs bowled by him.

Well that escalated quickly! The Lankans have lost their last 6 wickets for just 16 runs which means, New Zealand have gained a decent lead of 74 runs and it is courtesy Tent Boult. He leads the team off the field and to a standing ovation. He deserves every bit of it. He has been exceptional today morning. He has taken all the six wickets to fall this morning and in very, very quick time.

OUT! Three reds and that is the end of the Lankan innings! Boult finishes with a 6-fer. Not sure what Kumara was doing there. Boult bowls it full around the leg stump. Now I am not sure if Kumara was trying to move out of the way or he lost sight of the ball but he offered no shot. The ball hits him low on the pads. An appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger. Kumara being the last man takes the review but that is never going to save him as it is absolutely plumb. THE LANKANS HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 104!
Review time! However, that is absolutely plumb. It is a review in hope this. Kumara is the man in question.
Another play and a miss! Full and outside off, it shapes away. Kumara goes for the drive but misses the ball by a mile.
On a length around off, the batsman gets right behind the line and defends it onto the ground.
BEATEN! Full and around off, it shapes away. Kumara hangs his bat out and gets beaten.
Lahiru Kumara is the new batsman in.

OUT! Fifer for Boult! He does not get a hat-trick but gets Chameera on the next ball. It is bowled on a similar length and line like the hat-trick ball but it comes back in late. Chameera tries to defend but misses. It hits him on the front pad. An appeal and the umpire too agrees. New Zealand one wicket away now from taking a big lead. Boult has 4 balls to bowl to the last batsman.
No hat-trick as Chameera has defended it solidly. Good length around off, it is defended.
FOUR! Short of a length delivery, Mathews pulls it over square leg for a boundary. Good short stuff from Southee.
Short of a length delivery, Mathews looks to hook but misses it.
Good length delivery on off, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Good length delivery on middle, Mathews tucks it to the leg side.
Good length delivery on off, Mathews looks to defend but gets hit on the hand. That could be a nasty blow.
Good length delivery on middle, Mathews defends off the back foot.
Dushmantha Chameera is the new batsman in.

OUT! PLUMB IN FRONT! Two in two for Boult! His fourth today. Sri Lanka have slipped from 94 for 4 to 100 for 8. A corker of a yorker this from Boult. It also tails back in very late. Lakmal plays all around it, it hits him on the boot. An appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger. Lakmal bags a golden duck. Boult will be on a hat-trick in the next over. End of a triple-wicket over by Boult.
Suranga Lakmal is the new batsman in.

OUT! Three reds and Dilruwan has to continue his long walk back! One brings two and two brings three. Boult is on fire here. He has taken all the wickets to fall today morning. Another top nut. Boult lands it on a length around off, Dilruwan shapes up to leave it thinking it will slant away. The ball though jags back in sharply after pitching. Hits Perera on the pads. The player appeals and the umpire raises his finger. Dilruwan walks upto his partner and after a chat signals the 'T'. Replays show that the on-field call is the right one. Lanka lose a review and the Kiwis are now into the tail. A big lead is there for the taking for them now.
Dilruwan is a goner! He has been adjudged LBW but he has opted to review. Looks out.
Wide outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Good length on off, Perera keeps it out.
Good length on off, Perera pushes it to covers.
Dilruwan Perera is the new batsman in.

OUT! EDGED AND WHAT A CATCH! Once again it is the Boult-Southee combination. But a lot of credit has to be given to the latter. He has taken an absolute blinder. Trent bowls it full around off, it shapes away late. Dickwella goes after it with not much foot movement. The ball takes an outside edge and flies between second slip and third slip. Southee in the latter position dives and sticks his right hand out and the ball sticks. The Kiwis are ecstatic and they are right on top here. Sri Lanka trail by another 78 and have only 4 wickets in hand.
On a length around off, Mathews strokes it back to the bowler.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Good shot! Not a boundary but two! Full and on middle, Mathews just times it through mid on and takes a brace.
Slightly outside off, Mathews with not a lot of foot movement, keeps it out.
Good length again around off, Mathews defends it towards mid on.
Hits the length around off, Mathews defends it onto the ground.
Well left! Around off and it swings away. Dickwella covers his off pole and leaves it alone. End of a successful over by Boult.
FOUR! Off the mark in style. Full and on the pads, Dickwella flicks it uppishly but over the man at mid-wicket for a boundary.
Niroshan Dickwella is the new batsman in.

OUT! Boult strikes! A well-deserved wicket this. He has been brilliant this morning and has got the reward. However, there is nothing great about this delivery, it is full and outside off, Silva maybe could have left it. But he has been drawn into the stroke. He plays a half-hearted drive. The ball takes the outside edge and goes to Tim Southee at third slip. An early wicket for New Zealand and Sri Lanka now have half the side back in the hut.

A huge shout from the bowler but nothing from the keeper and the slip cordon. Back of a length around off, it takes off after pitching. Silva tries to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Well bowled and well played! Full and on off, it tails back in late. Silva adjusts and flicks it through mid-wicket and the batsmen run two.
On off and it angles away. Silva plays inside the line and lets it be.
Almost drags it on! Full and on off, Mathews goes for the drive away from his body but gets an inside edge onto his pads. A better over this from Southee.
OUCH! Goes wide of the crease and angles it into the batsman. Mathews tries to defend but misses to get hit near the box.
Wide outside off, left alone.
The surprise bouncer! Mathews though takes on the challenge of pulling but is beaten by the extra bounce.
Perfect! Length delivery and on off, it shapes away after pitching. Mathews tries to defend but it takes an outside edge and goes along the ground to gully.
Southee needs to be a little more straight here. For now, he is way too wide outside off. Mathews will keep leaving such deliveries and he does exactly that on this one.
Silva pushes it towards covers, he wants a run but is rightly sent back.
On a length and it is kept out.
The bouncer this time, good change in length. Boult ducks under it.
Fullish and on off, it comes back in. Silva strokes it to mid off.
BEATEN! Good length delivery angling on off, the ball skidded through and whizzed past the outside edge of Roshen Silva. Good bowling by Boult.
Full on off, Silva manages to defend it.
Outside off again and it is left alone. A maiden but not a threatening one.
Now the length was good but the line is outside off again. Mathews makes a leave.
Perfect line on off but the length is a little too full. Mathews strokes it to mid off.
Better this from Southee! Closer to the off pole but not close enough to make the batsman play.
Wayward start by Southee! He is getting some swing but the line is not right. It is once again way outside off, Mathews does not fiddle with it.
Swing straightaway for Southee but the line is a little too wide outside off. It swings away further. Mathews need not play at it.
Tim Southee to bowl from the other end.

FOUR! First runs of today! It comes off the edge. On a length and around off, it angles away. Silva plays inside the line, the ball takes the outside edge and races to the third man fence. A boundary to end the first over of the day but it was a testing one.
Hits the length hard on off, Silva defends it.
A little too wide outside off, Boult was trying to get the ball to curl back in. It does not and Silva lets it be.
Fuller again but no swing this time around off, Silva strokes it to covers.
Goes fuller this time and straightaway it causes problems! It tails back in a little from outside off, Silva tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Slightly short on off to begin with, hence not giving the ball a lot of time to swing. Goes straight on. Silva gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
We are all set for the action to begin with. Angelo Mathews and Roshen Silva are at the crease. Trent Boult will start the proceedings for Day 2.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the second Test between New Zealand and Sri Lanka in Christchurch. Day 1 saw both the teams on level terms. However, a couple of quick wickets, will see the Kiwis have the upper hand and that is exactly what Kane Williamson will be looking for. For Sri Lanka, one good partnership will see them gain the advantage. The first session is an important one, let us see how it pans out. Stay tuned.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

What can we expect on Day 2? The Kiwis will look to run through the middle and the lower order and gain some sort of a lead. The visitors, on the other hand, will hope the two batting out there can build a decent partnership and the ones to follow can also contribute after that. A lead for any side will be important and both the teams will know that. Who will get it? Join us to find out on Day 2 at 1100 local (2200 GMT, previous night). Till then, take care and goodbye!

Earlier in the day, the Lankans won the toss and put the Kiwis in to bat. The decision turned out to be the right one as they had New Zealand on the mat at 64 for 6 but could not capitalize. However, an attacking Southee and a resurgent Watling added a 108-run stand and brought the Kiwis back into the contest. Lakmal's fifer though kept the Lankans on the front foot. But impressive bowling from the hosts' bowlers has seen Day 1 end even-stevens.

A day dominated by the bowlers is what we have witnessed today. A total of 14 wickets have fallen and the game is evenly poised at the end of Day 1. The last session saw the Lankans take the remaining two Kiwi wickets quickly. In reply, they lost their top three in quick succession. Mendis and Mathews then did try to steady the ship but a lapse in concentration saw the departure of the former. Mathews though is still battling out there and he along with Roshen Silva are amidst a 37-run stand and they have brought the lead down to 10 short of 100.

NOT OUT! So, so close! Mathews survives on the final ball of the day! Good length delivery on middle, Mathews looked to defend but got hit on the pads. The bowler appealed but the umpire shook his head. After a bit of a discussion, New Zealand go for the review. Replays show that it was umpire's call in terms of height. Could have been given too! Nervy moment. THAT IS STUMPS ON DAY 1, SRI LANKA TRAIL BY 90!
A review on the last ball of the day! A huge appeal for LBW has been turned down. Mathews is the man in question. The Kiwis have gone for the review. Looks close. Height can be an issue.

OUT! IN THE AIR, TAKEN! Southee gets his third. Both openers have gone. That is a bad, bad shot from Gunathilaka. To take on the short delivery is fine but not without seeing it totally. He is neither at square leg nor in the deep. Somewhere in between. He first comes forward but then realizes that he has to go back. Backtracks a couple of steps quickly and takes it nicely. Sri Lanka slip further and still trail by 157 runs.

An appeal goes up and the umpire raises his finger. Sri Lanka in trouble here, they have lost two early wickets and trail by another 158 runs.
